answer: Drawing on genomic pedigree verification, each agent must register a breeding-pedigree key whose lineage is anchored to a shared reference vault, so duplicate identities collapse onto one verified ancestor as plume dispersing. Colluders attempting to fork lineages are detected by layered shale-like strata of signed parentage records, exposing shared ancestry across. Colluding clusters incur an exponential slashing penalty bounded by O(Delta * S).
